hindi: पर्वतीय विस्तार पर (जल) कटु और काली मिट्टी वाली (भूमि) पर मधुर होता है। पृथ्वी पर स्थित जल का यह षाड्गुण्य कहा गया है। उसी प्रकार जो ऐन्द्र, कार और हिम (जल) है, उसे अव्यक्त रस वाला जानना चाहिए।
english: On a mountain expanse (water) is pungent, on (ground) of black soil sweet. This sixfold nature (ṣāḍguṇya) of water lying on the earth has been declared. Likewise one should know that which is Indra's (aindra) water, hail (kāra) and snow (hima) as of unmanifest taste.
notes: Continues 199: the six tastes of water on the six kinds of ground make up the 'sixfold nature' (ṣāḍguṇya). This numbered verse has three printed lines. kāra is taken as hail; the word is not otherwise explained in the chunk. aindra = the water of rain, as in 196 and 201. hi is an expletive particle and is not rendered.

hindi: जो जल इन्द्र द्वारा छोड़ा हुआ आकाश से गिरता है और कहे गए पात्रों से ग्रहण किया जाता है, उसे धीर जन ऐन्द्र ही कहते हैं; वह राजाओं के पीने योग्य प्रधान जल है।
english: The water which falls from the sky released by Indra and is received in the vessels stated, that the wise call indeed Indra's (aindra), the chief water, to be drunk by kings.
notes: Upajāti metre (line 1: Upendravajrā + Indravajrā; line 2: Indravajrā); the weights fit as printed. 'The vessels stated' refers to vessels named earlier in the text, not in this chunk.

hindi: थोड़ा कषाय और मधुर, अति सूक्ष्म, विशद, लघु, अरूक्ष और अनभिष्यन्दी — ऐसा सब पानी उत्तम है।
english: Slightly astringent and sweet, very subtle, non-slimy, light, not dry and not channel-clogging: all such drinking water is the best.
notes: 'such' renders the relation of the qualities to sarvaṃ pānīyam; the sentence has no relative pronoun.

hindi: वर्षा ऋतु का नया पानी गुरु, अभिष्यन्दी और मधुर होता है; शरद् में जो बरसता है वह प्रायः तनु, लघु और अनभिष्यन्दी होता है।
english: Fresh water of the Varṣā season is heavy, channel-clogging and sweet; (the water that) rains in Śarad is mostly thin, light and not channel-clogging.

text_flags.why: 'ladhu' is not a word; the pair guru (this line) / laghu (202, 205 'laghutaraṃ') and the sense 'light' need laghu (gh for dh); syllable count is the same

notes: Varṣā = the rains, Śarad = autumn (season equivalents). prāyaḥ 'mostly' may also go with varṣati ('what mostly rains in Śarad'); the qualities are given first. The subject of varṣati is not printed.

hindi: वह (शरद् का जल) तो, जो सुकुमार हों और जिनका भोजन अधिकतर स्निग्ध हो, उनके भोज्य, भक्ष्य, लेह्य और पेय में प्रशस्त है।
english: That (water of Śarad), for those who are delicate and whose food is mostly unctuous, is recommended in their food, eatables, lickables and drinks.
notes: tat refers back to the Śarad water of 203. bhojya/bhakṣya/lehya/peya are the four kinds of food (to be eaten, chewed, licked, drunk); the literal words are given.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: हेमन्त में जल स्निग्ध, वृष्य, बल के लिए हितकर और गुरु होता है; शिशिर में उससे कुछ लघुतर और कफ तथा वात को जीतने वाला होता है।
english: In Hemanta water is unctuous, aphrodisiac, good for strength and heavy; in Śiśira it is slightly lighter than that and conquers Kapha and Vāta.
notes: Hemanta = early winter, Śiśira = late winter (season equivalents).

hindi: वसन्त के जल को कषाय, मधुर और रूक्ष जानना चाहिए; परन्तु ग्रीष्म का जल अनभिष्यन्दी होता है — यही निश्चय है।
english: One should know the water of Vasanta as astringent and sweet and dry; but the water of Grīṣma is not channel-clogging: this indeed is the settled conclusion.
notes: Vasanta = spring, Grīṣma = summer (season equivalents).

hindi: परन्तु अव्यवस्थित ऋतुओं में बादल जो जल देते हैं, वह दोष के लिए होता है, इसमें संशय नहीं।
english: But the water which clouds give in disordered seasons leads to harm (doṣa); there is no doubt about this.
notes: doṣāya yujyate, literally 'is joined to doṣa', is taken as 'leads to harm'; doṣa may also mean the bodily doṣas here (it vitiates them). The second tu is resumptive and is not rendered.

hindi: राजाओं, राजा के समान (व्यक्तियों) और सुकुमार मनुष्यों को शरद् में भली-भाँति संगृहीत जल विशेष रूप से प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
english: By kings, those of kingly rank and delicate men the waters of Śarad, well collected, should be used especially.
notes: rājamātra 'of the measure of a king' is taken as persons of kingly rank. śaradyāpaḥ is split śaradi āpaḥ (i + ā = yā).

words.gloss: whose waters are broken, agitated and struck by stones

hindi: जिन नदियों का जल पत्थरों से टूटता, विक्षुब्ध होता और टकराता है, वे हिमवान् से निकलने वाली नदियाँ पथ्य, पुण्य और देवर्षियों से सेवित हैं।
english: Rivers rising in Himavat, whose waters are broken, agitated and struck by stones, are wholesome, holy and frequented by divine sages.
notes: Himavat is kept as the printed place name. pāṣāṇa 'by stones' is taken with all three participles.

words.gram: f. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: और जो नदियाँ पत्थर और बालू बहाने वाली, निर्मल जल वाली और मलय से निकलने वाली हैं, उनमें जल अमृत के समान होता है।
english: And the rivers which carry stones and sand, with clear water, and rise in Malaya: the water in them is like amṛta (nectar).
notes: Malaya is kept as the printed place name.

hindi: और जो (नदियाँ) पश्चिम की ओर बहती हैं, वे निर्मल जल वाली और पथ्य हैं; और जो पूर्व समुद्र में जाती हैं, वे प्रायः मन्द बहने वाली और गुरु होती हैं।
english: And those (rivers) which face west are wholesome, with clean water; and those which go to the eastern sea mostly flow gently and are heavy.
notes: mṛduvaha 'flowing gently' may also mean 'carrying soft (water)'; the first is given.

words.gram: f. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: of head disease, heart disease and kuṣṭha

hindi: जो (नदियाँ) पारियात्र से और जो विन्ध्य तथा सह्य से निकलती हैं, वे शिरोरोग, हृद्रोग, कुष्ठ और श्लीपद का कारण हैं।
english: The (rivers) which arise in Pāriyātra and those which arise in Vindhya and Sahya are the cause of head disease, heart disease, kuṣṭha and ślīpada.
notes: Pāriyātra, Vindhya and Sahya are kept as the printed place names. śiro-hṛdroga is taken as 'head disease and heart disease' (roga shared). The predicate hetuḥ stays singular with the plural subject tāḥ, as a predicate noun may. kuṣṭha and ślīpada are kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: whose waters are polluted by earth, insects, snakes, rats and filth

hindi: जिन नदियों का जल मिट्टी, कीड़ों, साँपों, चूहों और मल से दूषित है और जो वर्षा का जल बहाती हैं, वे सब दोषों को उभारने वाली हैं।
english: Rivers whose waters are polluted by earth, insects, snakes, rats and filth, and which carry rain-water, stir up all the doṣas.
notes: vasudhā-kīṭa may also be one item, 'earth-insects'; the list reading is given. samīraṇa is taken as 'stirring up' (from sam-√īr), not as Vāta.

words.gloss: in tanks, wells, ponds, springs, lakes, cascades and the rest
words.gram: m./n. loc. pl., bahuvrīhi (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: of marsh, mountain and dry region

hindi: वापी, कूप, तडाग, उत्स, सरोवर, प्रस्रवण आदि में (जल को) आनूप, पर्वतीय और धन्व देश के गुण-दोषों से जानना चाहिए।
english: In tanks (vāpī), wells, ponds, springs (utsa), lakes, cascades (prasravaṇa) and the rest, one should determine (the water) by the merits and defects of marsh, mountain and dry region (dhanvan).
notes: The object (water) is understood. guṇa-doṣa here = merits and defects (not the bodily doṣas).

hindi: जो जल पिच्छिल, कृमियों से युक्त, पत्तों, शैवाल और कीचड़ से क्लिन्न, विवर्ण, विरस, गाढ़ा और दुर्गन्ध वाला हो, वह हितकर नहीं है।
english: Water that is slimy, full of worms (krimi), soaked with leaves, moss (śaivāla) and mud, discoloured, ill-tasting, thick and foul-smelling is not wholesome.
notes: parṇa-śaivāla-kardamaiḥ is taken with klinnam.

hindi: जो जल वरुणालय का है, वह विस्र, त्रिदोषकारक और लवण होता है। इस प्रकार यह आठवाँ, भली-भाँति निश्चित, जलवर्ग कहा गया।
english: The water which belongs to the abode of Varuṇa (the sea) is of raw-flesh smell (visra), provokes the three doṣas and is salty. This eighth group, of waters, well established, has been declared.
notes: varuṇālaya 'abode of Varuṇa' is the sea; the word is used as an adjective of ambu. tridoṣa is taken as 'provoking all three doṣas' (literally 'having the three doṣas'). iti closes the group and is not rendered separately in the English.

hindi: अब गोरसवर्ग — गाय का दूध दस गुणों वाला है: मधुर, शीत, मृदु, स्निग्ध, बहल, श्लक्ष्ण, पिच्छिल, गुरु, मन्द और प्रसन्न।
english: Now the group of milk products (gorasa): cow's milk has ten qualities: sweet, cold, soft, unctuous, thick, smooth, slimy, heavy, slow and clear.
notes: The heading 'atha gorasavargaḥ' is printed at the head of the verse line, outside the metre (the line without it has 16 syllables); the dashes are left out of the split. The ten qualities are counted: svādu, śīta, mṛdu, snigdha, bahala, ślakṣṇa, picchila, guru, manda, prasanna.

hindi: वह (दूध) सामान्य के कारण ऐसे ही गुणों वाले ओज को बढ़ाता है। दूध जीवनीयों में श्रेष्ठ और रसायन कहा गया है।
english: That (milk), through sameness (sāmānya), increases ojas (the vital essence), which has just such qualities. Milk is declared the foremost of vitalizing things and a rejuvenative (rasāyana).
notes: tat is taken as the subject (the milk of 217); it could also be read 'therefore'. evaṃguṇam eva qualifies ojas: ojas has the same qualities as the milk. abhivardhayet (optative) is rendered as a general statement.

words.gloss: for one with excessive digestive fire

hindi: भैंसों का दूध गाय के दूध से गुरुतर और शीततर है, स्नेह में कम नहीं है; वह अनिद्रा वाले के लिए और अत्यधिक अग्नि वाले के लिए हितकर है।
english: The milk of she-buffaloes is heavier and colder than cow's (milk) and not deficient in fat; it is wholesome for one without sleep and for one with excessive digestive fire (agni).
notes: sneha-anyūnam is split 'not deficient in fat' (sneha + anyūna); a split snehāt + nyūnam 'less than in fat' would need the printed form snehānnyūnam.

words.gloss: for Vāta, Kapha, ānāha, worms, swelling, udara and arśas

hindi: ऊँटनियों का दूध रूक्ष, उष्ण, थोड़ा लवण और लघु है; वह वात, कफ, आनाह, कृमि, शोफ, उदर और अर्श में प्रशस्त है।
english: The milk of she-camels is dry and hot, slightly salty and light; it is recommended for Vāta, Kapha, distension (ānāha), worms (krimi), swelling (śopha), udara and arśas.
notes: udara and arśas are kept Sanskrit.

hindi: एक खुर वाले (पशुओं) का सब दूध बल्य, स्थिरता करने वाला और उष्ण है; वह अम्लता सहित, लवणता सहित, रूक्ष, शाखा के वात को हरने वाला और लघु है।
english: All milk of one-hoofed (animals) is strengthening, gives firmness, and is hot; it is somewhat sour and somewhat salty, dry, removes Vāta in the periphery (śākhā), and is light.
notes: caikaśaphaṃ is split ca + aikaśapham (derived adjective 'of one-hoofed animals'); ca + ekaśapham would give the same printed form. sa-amla, sa-lavaṇa 'with sourness, with saltiness' are rendered 'somewhat sour, somewhat salty'.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: बकरी का दूध कषाय और मधुर, शीत, ग्राही और लघु है; वह रक्तपित्त और अतिसार का नाशक तथा क्षय, कास और ज्वर को दूर करने वाला है।
english: Goat's milk is astringent and sweet, cold, binding and light; it destroys raktapitta and diarrhoea (atisāra) and removes kṣaya (wasting), cough and fever.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: परन्तु भेड़ का (दूध) उष्ण, हिक्का और श्वास करने वाला तथा पित्त और श्लेष्मा को बढ़ाने वाला है। हथिनियों का दूध बल्य, गुरु और परम स्थिरता करने वाला है।
english: But sheep's (milk) is hot, causes hiccup (hikkā) and dyspnoea, and increases Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman). The milk of she-elephants is strengthening, heavy, and gives firmness supremely.
notes: param may also be an adjective of payaḥ ('excellent'); it is taken adverbially with sthairyakaram.

hindi: मनुष्य का दूध जीवन देने वाला, बृंहण, सात्म्य और स्नेहन है; वह रक्तपित्त में नावन है और नेत्र-शूल वालों के लिए तर्पण है।
english: Human milk is vitalizing, nourishing, suitable (sātmya) and oleating (snehana); in raktapitta it is nasal therapy (nāvana), and for those with eye-pain (śūla) it is a tarpaṇa (replenishing application).
notes: tarpaṇa is the replenishing application for the eyes; kept Sanskrit.

hindi: दही रोचन, दीपन, वृष्य, स्नेहन, बल बढ़ाने वाला, पाक में अम्ल, उष्ण, वात का नाशक, मङ्गल्य और बृंहण है।
english: Curd (dadhi) promotes relish (rocana), stimulates digestion, is aphrodisiac, oleating, increases strength, is sour in vipāka, hot, Vāta-destroying, auspicious and nourishing.
notes: pāke = in vipāka.

hindi: पीनस में, अतिसार में, शीतक में, विषमज्वर में, अरुचि में, मूत्रकृच्छ्र में और कृशता में दही प्रशस्त है।
english: Curd is recommended in pīnasa, in diarrhoea, in śītaka, in irregular fever, in loss of taste (aruci), in mūtrakṛcchra and in emaciation.
notes: śītaka (literally 'cold') is kept Sanskrit; it may also be read as an adjective of viṣamajvare ('irregular fever with chills'); the list reading is given. pīnasa and mūtrakṛcchra are kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: arising from blood, Pitta and Kapha
words.gram: m. loc. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: शरद्, ग्रीष्म और वसन्त में दही प्रायः निन्दित है, और रक्त, पित्त और कफ से उत्पन्न विकारों में वह अहितकर है।
english: In Śarad, Grīṣma and Vasanta curd is generally condemned; and it is unwholesome in disorders arising from blood, Pitta and Kapha.
notes: rakta-pitta-kapha may also be read raktapitta + kapha ('arising from raktapitta and Kapha'); the three-member reading is given.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: मन्दक त्रिदोषकारक है; जमा हुआ दही वात का नाशक है; सर शुक्र बढ़ाने वाला है; परन्तु मण्ड श्लेष्मा और अनिल का नाशक और स्रोतों का शोधक है।
english: Mandaka provokes the three doṣas; formed curd destroys Vāta; the sara (upper layer) increases semen; but the maṇḍa (the liquid part) destroys Kapha (śleṣman) and Vāta (anila) and cleanses the channels (srotas).
notes: mandaka, sara and maṇḍa are stages or parts of curd (dadhi) and are kept Sanskrit; the glosses are literal ('slow/weak', 'flowing/upper part', 'liquid part'). tridoṣa is taken as 'provoking all three doṣas', as in 216. The commas are printed and left out of the split.

words.gloss: in swelling, arśas, grahaṇī disorder, retention of urine, udara and loss of taste
words.gram: f. loc. sg., dvandva (last member aruci)

hindi: शोफ, अर्श, ग्रहणी-दोष, मूत्र-ग्रह, उदर, अरुचि, स्नेह-व्यापद्, पाण्डुत्व और गरों में तक्र देना चाहिए।
english: One should give buttermilk (takra) in swelling (śopha), arśas, grahaṇī disorder, retention of urine (mūtragraha), udara and loss of taste (aruci), in ill effects of fat (snehavyāpad), in pallor and in gara.
notes: The long compound ends in the feminine locative singular of aruci; it is taken as a list (dvandva). grahaṇī, arśas, udara and gara are kept Sanskrit.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., karmadhāraya, ppp. ud-√hṛ

words.gloss: destroying disorders of grahaṇī and arśas
words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: removing ardita and loss of taste
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: ताज़ा निकाला हुआ नवनीत संग्राही, दीपन और हृद्य है; वह ग्रहणी और अर्श के विकारों का नाशक तथा अर्दित और अरुचि को नष्ट करने वाला है।
english: Butter (navanīta) freshly taken out is binding, stimulates digestion and is pleasing to the heart (hṛdya); it destroys disorders of grahaṇī and arśas and removes ardita and loss of taste (aruci).
notes: grahaṇī, arśas and ardita are kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: increasing memory, intellect, digestive fire, semen, ojas, Kapha and fat
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: removing Vāta, Pitta, poison, insanity, śoṣa, misfortune and fever
words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: (घृत) स्मृति, बुद्धि, अग्नि, शुक्र, ओज, कफ और मेद को बढ़ाने वाला तथा वात, पित्त, विष, उन्माद, शोष, अलक्ष्मी और ज्वर को दूर करने वाला है;
english: (Ghee) increases memory, intellect, digestive fire (agni), semen, ojas, Kapha and fat (medas), and removes Vāta, Pitta, poison, insanity (unmāda), śoṣa (wasting), misfortune (alakṣmī) and fever;
notes: SENTENCE: the unit has no noun; it is taken with ghṛtam in 232, which carries the sentence on (the neuter adjectives could also continue navanītam of 230). śoṣa is kept Sanskrit.

hindi: सब स्नेहों में उत्तम, शीत, रस और पाक में मधुर घृत विधियों से सहस्र वीर्य वाला और सहस्र कर्म करने वाला है।
english: Ghee (ghṛta) is the best of all fats, cold, sweet in taste (rasa) and vipāka; by (its) methods (of preparation) it has a thousand potencies (vīrya) and does a thousand actions.
notes: vidhibhiḥ 'by methods' is taken with both sahasravīryam and karmasahasrakṛt; the processing of ghee with other drugs is meant. pāka beside rasa = vipāka.

words.gloss: mada, apasmāra, mūrcchāya, śoṣa, insanity, gara and fevers
pain of the yoni, ear and head
words.gram: n. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: पुराना घृत मद, अपस्मार, मूर्च्छा, शोष, उन्माद, गर और ज्वरों को तथा योनि, कान और सिर के शूल को दूर करता है।
english: Old ghee removes mada, apasmāra, mūrcchāya, śoṣa, insanity (unmāda), gara and fevers, and pain of the yoni, ear and head.

text_flags.why: 'mūrcchsāya' is not a word and 'rcchs' is not a possible cluster here; the list of disorders (mada, apasmāra ...) needs mūrcchāya (stray s); syllable count is the same (16)

notes: mada, apasmāra, mūrcchāya, śoṣa and gara are kept Sanskrit; yoni is kept Sanskrit (the female genital part).

words.gloss: like the milk of goat, sheep and she-buffalo

hindi: बकरी, भेड़ और भैंस के अपने-अपने घृतों को उनके दूध के समान बताना चाहिए। पीयूष, मोरट और जो विविध किलाट हैं,
english: One should declare the ghees, each of its own (animal), to be like the milk of goat, sheep and she-buffalo. Pīyūṣa and moraṭa, and the various kilāṭas which (there are),
notes: svāni 'their own' is taken with sarpīṃṣi: each animal's ghee is like that animal's milk. pīyūṣa, moraṭa and kilāṭa are milk preparations of the gorasa group and are kept Sanskrit. SENTENCE: line 2 runs into 235 (sarva eva sukhapradāḥ). caiva: eva is taken as 'also' after ca and is not rendered separately.

words.gloss: for those with intense digestive fire

hindi: वे सब ही तीव्र अग्नि वालों और अनिद्रा वालों को सुख देने वाले, गुरु, तर्पण, वृष्य, बृंहण और पवन को दूर करने वाले हैं।
english: all of these indeed give comfort to those with intense digestive fire and to the sleepless; they are heavy, replenishing (tarpaṇa), aphrodisiac, nourishing and remove Vāta (pavana).

text_flags.why: metre: the first quarter has 9 syllables as printed (dī-pa-tā-gnī-nā-ma-ni-drā-ṇāṃ), 8 with dīpta; 'dīpata' is not a word, dīpta 'blazing' gives 'those with intense digestive fire'

notes: Continues 234: the subject is pīyūṣa, moraṭa and the kilāṭas. sarva is split sarve (e lost before the vowel of eva, as printed). dīpta-agni 'one whose digestive fire is intense' is a bahuvrīhi.

hindi: तक्रपिण्डक विशद, गुरु, रूक्ष और ग्राही होते हैं। गोरसों का यह नौवाँ वर्ग कहा गया।
english: Buttermilk lumps (takrapiṇḍaka) are non-slimy, heavy, dry and binding. This ninth group, of milk products (gorasa), has been declared.
notes: takrapiṇḍaka is kept Sanskrit with a literal gloss.

hindi: अब इक्षुवर्ग — चबाए हुए ईख का रस वृष्य, शीत, सर, स्निग्ध, बृंहण, मधुर और श्लेष्मल होता है; परन्तु यन्त्र से निकाला हुआ (रस) विदाह करता है।
english: Now the group of sugarcane (ikṣu): the juice of sugarcane that is chewed is aphrodisiac, cold, laxative (sara), unctuous, nourishing, sweet and increases Kapha; but (the juice) from the press (yāntrika) turns burning (vidahyate).

text_flags.why: 'okṣu' is not a word; atha + ikṣu gives athekṣu, and the same unit names the sugarcane as ikṣoḥ (line 2); syllable count is the same

notes: The heading 'atha ikṣuvargaḥ' is printed at the head of the verse line, outside the metre (the line without it has 16 syllables); the dashes are left out of the split. vidahyate (passive of vi-√dah) is taken as 'undergoes burning (vidāha)' in digestion; Hindi विदाह.

words.gloss: producing abundant worms, marrow, blood, fat and flesh
words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: शीतलता, प्रसाद और माधुर्य के कारण वंशक पौण्ड्रक से श्रेष्ठ है। गुड़ बहुत कृमि, मज्जा, रक्त, मेद और मांस करने वाला है।
english: In coolness, clarity and sweetness vaṃśaka is better than pauṇḍraka. Guḍa produces abundant worms (krimi), marrow, blood, fat (medas) and flesh.

text_flags.why: grammar: the abstract noun 'sweetness' is mādhurya (vṛddhi, like śaitya from śīta in the same line); madhurya is not a word; the 6th syllable becomes heavy (ma-vipulā instead of ra-vipulā), both allowed
possible: 'nodo' is not a word; a list of body tissues (majjā, asṛk, māṃsa) needs medas 'fat', as in 231 '...kaphamedovivardhanam'; asṛk + medo gives asṛṅmedo; syllable count is the same

notes: pauṇḍraka and vaṃśaka are kinds of sugarcane named in the ikṣu group; kept Sanskrit. guḍa = jaggery (common name). prabhūta 'abundant' is taken with all the members of the compound.

words.gloss: reduced to a quarter, a third or a half
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member), ppp. caus. ava-√śiṣ

hindi: क्षुद्र गुड़ वह रस है जो चौथाई, तिहाई या आधा शेष रहने तक (पकाया गया) हो; वह (इनमें) पहले-पहले वाला अधिक गुरु होता है। धोया हुआ गुड़ बहुत कम मल वाला होता है।
english: Minor (kṣudra) guḍa is the juice reduced to a quarter, a third or a half; (of these) each preceding one is heavier. Washed guḍa has very little dirt (mala).
notes: The grammar of line 1 + rasaḥ is loose: rasaḥ ... avaśeṣitaḥ 'juice left as a remainder' is taken as defining kṣudra guḍa; it may also be read as two items (kṣudra guḍa; and the juice reduced to a quarter, a third or a half). guruḥ yathāpūrvam: the first-named (reduced to a quarter) is the heaviest. 'boiled' is understood in the Hindi bracket. mala here = dirt (impurity of the guḍa).
